KEY MESSAGE 1...Periods of unsettled weather are expected
through Friday.

Aloft, cyclonic WNW'erly flow and embedded shortwave troughs
affect our region through Friday as a longwave trough axis 
moves from eastern NY and vicinity to near the western Canadian
Maritimes by sunset Friday evening. At the surface, a weak trough 
lingers over the eastern Great Lakes and vicinity, including 
our CWA, through this early evening. During tonight through 
Friday, a high pressure ridge should build gradually from the 
western Great Lakes. Net low-level CAA on the synoptic-scale
persists through Friday. Late afternoon highs should reach 
mainly the mid 50's to mid 60's today and the lower 50's to mid
60's on Friday amidst a primarily mainly clear to partly cloudy
sky. In between, overnight lows should reach mainly the upper 
30's to mid 40's around daybreak Friday.

Primarily fair weather is expected through nightfall Friday
evening. However, periodic lake-effect rain showers should occur
over/downwind of ~16C Lake America, especially this evening
through Friday afternoon, amidst a W'erly to WNW'erly mean low-level
flow of sufficiently-cold/moist air (e.g. 850 mb temperatures
near 3C) and weak to moderate lake-induced CAPE. These lake-effect 
rain showers should be focused across Oswego County, the Tug 
Hill Plateau, and vicinity. Note: the low-level air mass should
remain insufficiently-cold for lake-effect rain showers
over/downwind of Lake Erie during this latest spell of cold
weather. Outside the lake-effect precip, isolated rain showers 
are possible through this early evening, especially across the 
Niagara Frontier, Finger Lakes, and North- Central NY, and 
during Friday afternoon, especially across North-Central NY as 
weak boundary layer CAPE, stemming from daytime warming amidst 
sufficient low- level moisture, should be released by low-level 
convergence/moist ascent along surface trough axes attendant to 
shortwave troughs aloft. A few thunderstorms are possible across
North-Central NY this afternoon through early evening, when 
weak surface-based MUCAPE profiles should exhibit MUCAPE of at 
least 200 J/kg in the primarily electrical charge separation 
zone (i.e. the portion of the MUCAPE profile that spans the 
cumuliform cloud temperature range of 0C to -20C). Precip 
should end by sunset Friday evening, as the boundary layer 
stabilizes via nocturnal cooling and lake-induced CAPE wanes via
synoptic-scale low-level dry air advection and a lowering 
subsidence inversion that will accompany the aforementioned 
surface ridge. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...The remnants of Hurricane Isaias will bring a 
soaking rain to the region Sunday into early Monday.

Dry weather is expected this Friday night through Saturday as
the ridge at the surface and then aloft continues to build and
then crests E'ward across our CWA and vicinity, and is 
accompanied by stabilizing subsidence. Despite the development 
of weak net low-level WAA on the backside of the surface ridge 
Friday night, mainly clear sky, weak surface winds, and low 
humidity should allow overnight lows to reach mainly the mid 
30's to lower 40's around daybreak. The coldest lows are
expected in Lewis County. Strengthening net low-level WAA and 
daytime heating should allow late afternoon highs to reach the 
upper 50's to upper 60's in North-Central NY and the mid 60's to
mid 70's elsewhere in our CWA.

During Saturday night, ridging at the surface and aloft should
exit slowly E'ward from Western and Central NY as Isaias' 
remnant and vertically-stacked low at the surface and aloft, 
embedded in a trough aloft, wobbles NNE'ward across the western
TN Valley and toward the Lower OH Valley. Isolated rain showers
are possible, especially after midnight and across the Western 
Southern Tier, in response to moist isentropic ascent aloft 
generated by the low pressure system. Continued net low-level 
WAA and increasing cloud cover will limit nocturnal cooling. 
Lows should reach mainly the upper 40's to upper 50's around 
daybreak Sunday. On Sunday, the ridge at the surface and aloft 
should continue to exit slowly E'ward from our CWA as the 
aforementioned and vertically-stacked low at the surface and 
aloft wobbles NE'ward from near the Lower OH Valley toward the 
central Appalachians and the trough axis aloft approaches our
CWA from the western Great Lakes and vicinity. Widespread rain,
steady to heavy at times, should overspread our CWA generally 
from south to north as isentropic ascent aloft continues over 
our region and taps into abundant moisture originating over the 
southern Gulf Stream. Daytime highs should reach the 60's amidst
continued net low-level WAA. 

During Sunday night through nightfall Monday evening, the trough
axis aloft should move from the central Great Lakes and central
Appalachians toward the Canadian Maritimes and Atlantic waters
east of the Delmarva Peninsula. The vertically-stacked surface
low should dissipate in vicinity of the Mid OH Valley
